name: Outpatients and clinics
oneLine: Shows referrals, bookings, waiting lists and clinic days in one place.
today: Referrals often sit in inboxes and paper books, with no single waiting list. Patients are often all booked for the start of clinic, slots go unfilled, and missed appointments are rarely followed up.
todaySystem: A booking system holds the appointments, but waits inside the clinic and the reasons for empty slots often go unrecorded.
withOspeli: Every referral lands on one list with its wait shown. Clinic templates set slots and check-in times are logged, so waits, empty slots and missed appointments show clearly. Reminders are planned, not built yet.

people.does: Checks patients in by patient code on a tablet, marks arrived, seen or missed appointment.
Works the referral list, books slots from templates, rebooks cancellations. Sending reminders is planned, not built yet.
Calls the next patient from the clinic queue on a phone, marks start and finish.
Reviews waiting lists, slot use and clinic start times; adjusts templates.
Sees waits by service and clinics cancelled or running short.

screens.name: Clinic queue (phone)
screens.shows: Today's patients by patient code: booked time, arrived, waiting time, called, finished.

screens.name: Referral and waiting list
screens.shows: All open referrals by service and wait, unbooked first, with oldest waits highlighted.

screens.name: Clinic templates
screens.shows: Slot patterns per clinic and day, new and follow-up slots, held and released slots.

screens.name: Clinic day summary
screens.shows: Slots used, empty, cancelled and missed, start time and overrun per clinic.

captures: Referral received and accepted: starts the waiting-time clock.
Appointment booked, rebooked or cancelled, with who cancelled: shows churn.
Reminder sent and reply (planned, not built yet): will link reminders to attendance.
Patient arrived and checked in: starts the in-clinic wait.
Called in and consultation finished: measures in-clinic wait and clinic overrun.
Missed appointment recorded: drives the missed appointment rate and rebooking.
Clinic cancelled or reduced at short notice, with reason: shows lost capacity.

kpis.name: Missed appointment rate
kpis.definition: Clinic appointments marked "Missed appointment", divided by clinic appointments due in the period. Clinic sessions only: a home visit or outreach day is never counted here. The follow-up after a missed appointment is measured elsewhere.
kpis.numerator: Clinic appointments marked missed (the patient never arrived; recorded only after the booked time plus the grace, an example setting of 15 minutes).
kpis.denominator: Clinic appointments whose booked time is in the period.
kpis.exclusions: Appointments cancelled before the day of the appointment (site date). A patient who arrived and then left is not missed.

kpis.name: Slot utilisation
kpis.definition: Clinic slots used, divided by clinic slots released, for clinic sessions held in the period, after any reduction. A missed appointment counts as used: the slot could not be given to anyone else. Not the same as theatre session utilisation.
kpis.numerator: Slots with a booking that kept its place (attended, missed, or arrived and left).
kpis.denominator: Released slots of clinic sessions marked held, after reductions.
kpis.exclusions: Cancelled sessions, sessions not yet marked held, and sessions not released for booking.

kpis.name: Referral to first appointment
kpis.definition: Days between "Referral accepted" and the first finished clinic visit of the same patient code, median, in all and by service, for codes whose first visit finished in the period. Shown with the number still waiting.
kpis.numerator: Codes whose first finished visit after the referral was accepted falls in the period.
kpis.exclusions: Referrals with no finished visit yet: they are counted as "still waiting" beside the median, never hidden. A service with fewer than 5 codes shows no median (small-number rule, an example setting).

kpis.name: Waiting time in clinic
kpis.definition: Minutes between "Arrived" and "Called in", median, in all and by clinic, for patients called in the period.
kpis.numerator: Clinic appointments called in the period that were marked arrived first.
kpis.exclusions: Patients not called yet (shown live on the queue), and patients closed as "Seen, no times" with no call time (their number is shown beside it). A clinic with fewer than 5 patients called shows no median (small-number rule, an example setting).

kpis.name: Clinic start punctuality
kpis.definition: Clinic sessions held in the period whose first patient was called no later than 15 minutes after the planned start (earlier counts as on time), divided by clinic sessions held in which anyone was called. The 15-minute window is an example setting, not a standard.
kpis.numerator: Sessions held whose first "Called in" came within 15 minutes of the planned start, or before it.
kpis.denominator: Clinic sessions marked held in the period with at least one patient called.
kpis.exclusions: Sessions held in which nobody was called, and sessions held whose patients were all closed as "Seen, no times" with no call time (each number is shown beside it), cancelled sessions and sessions not yet marked held. A session counted late on its first recorded call, where a patient seen with no times arrived before that call, may have started on time: their number is shown beside it.

guide: When a clinic's missed appointment rate rises above its usual range, suggests a review of how that clinic books, citing recent weeks (extra reminders once reminders are built; they are planned).
When slots stay empty within two days of clinic, suggests offering them to the longest waiting referrals for that service.
When patients are all booked for the clinic start, suggests a staggered template, showing the current arrival-to-called waits.
playbooks: Waiting list validation: check each open referral, output list cleaned and contacted.
Clinic template review: compare demand and slots, output a revised template.

standards.how: Waiting-list and clinic records are designed to be usable as evidence when your organisation prepares for this chapter.

standards.name: HL7 FHIR Appointment, Slot and Schedule resources (planned)
standards.how: Export of bookings and clinic slots in this format is planned, not built.

notFor: Does not decide clinical urgency of referrals or who needs follow-up. Never times or ranks individual clinicians.

name: Emergency department flow
oneLine: Shows every wait in the emergency department, from arrival to departure.
today: Times are often written on paper, or not recorded. Ambulances can wait at the door, cubicles fill with patients waiting for ward beds, and it is hard to say where the hours went.
todaySystem: A tracking system records arrival and departure, but the waits between steps, and what each one was waiting for, are often hard to see.
withOspeli: Each stage is a timestamped tap: arrival, triage, seen, decision, bed requested, departed. A live board shows waits and blocks, and admission requests reach the bed board at once.

people.does: Sees the live board, logs arrivals and stage changes, raises escalation in two taps.
Records triage time and the category staff assigned, on a phone.
Sees decisions to admit waiting for beds and matches them on the bed board.
Sees handover status and time waiting at the door.
Watches crowding, long waits and escalation level; leads the full-capacity response.

screens.name: Department board
screens.shows: Patients by patient code and area: stage, time since arrival, waiting for what.

screens.name: Log a stage (phone)
screens.shows: Pick a patient code, tap the next stage; time is stamped automatically.

screens.name: Waiting for a bed
screens.shows: Decisions to admit by specialty, time waiting, bed requested and bed offered.

screens.name: Ambulance handover
screens.shows: Ambulances arrived, handed over and still waiting, with time at the door.

screens.name: Escalation status
screens.shows: Current crowding level, triggers met, actions taken and who decided.

captures: Arrival and arrival mode: starts every time measure.
Ambulance arrived and handover completed: measures time at the door.
Triage time and staff-assigned category: measures time to triage.
First seen by a clinician: measures time to be seen.
Decision to admit and bed requested: starts the wait for a bed.
Departure and destination, or left before being seen: ends the stay.
Escalation level changed, with triggers and decision maker: records the response.

kpis.name: Time in department (arrival → departure), share within the local standard
kpis.definition: attendances departing within the locally set time from arrival / all attendances
kpis.numerator: Attendances departing within the locally set time from arrival
kpis.statistic: Share (%), per period, with the median and 90th percentile time
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own
kpis.source: Welch et al. 2011, "Emergency department operational metrics, measures and definitions", Ann Emerg Med, PMID 21067846, doi:10.1016/j.annemergmed.2010.08.040 (consensus definitions; time limits are set locally); the time standard itself is set by each site

kpis.name: Time to triage
kpis.definition: arrival → triage recorded, median
kpis.numerator: Time between the two events, for each case
kpis.denominator: Cases with both times recorded in the period
kpis.statistic: Median, with the 90th percentile and n
kpis.exclusions: Cases missing either time are not counted; their number is shown beside the result
kpis.source: Welch et al. 2011, "Emergency department operational metrics, measures and definitions", Ann Emerg Med, PMID 21067846, doi:10.1016/j.annemergmed.2010.08.040 (consensus definitions; time limits are set locally)

kpis.name: Decision to admit to departure
kpis.definition: decision to admit → left the department, median and over 12 hours
kpis.numerator: Time between the two events, for each case
kpis.denominator: Cases with both times recorded in the period
kpis.statistic: Median, with the 90th percentile, n, and the number over 12 hours
kpis.exclusions: Cases missing either time are not counted; their number is shown beside the result
kpis.source: Welch et al. 2011, "Emergency department operational metrics, measures and definitions", Ann Emerg Med, PMID 21067846, doi:10.1016/j.annemergmed.2010.08.040 (consensus definitions; time limits are set locally)

kpis.name: Ambulance handover time
kpis.definition: ambulance arrived → handover completed, median and over the local limit
kpis.numerator: Time between the two events, for each case
kpis.denominator: Cases with both times recorded in the period
kpis.statistic: Median and over the local limit
kpis.exclusions: Cases missing either time are not counted; their number is shown beside the result

kpis.name: Left before being seen
kpis.definition: attendances leaving before first seen / all attendances
kpis.numerator: Attendances leaving before first seen
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own
kpis.source: Welch et al. 2011, "Emergency department operational metrics, measures and definitions", Ann Emerg Med, PMID 21067846, doi:10.1016/j.annemergmed.2010.08.040 (consensus definitions; time limits are set locally)

guide: When decisions to admit wait longer than the set limit, suggests a bed meeting review, listing waits by specialty from the bed board.
When crowding triggers are met, suggests the matching escalation level and actions for the charge nurse to confirm.
When ambulances wait beyond the local handover limit, alerts the operations manager with current cubicle and corridor use.
playbooks: Department flow walk: time each stage, output the biggest wait.
Full-capacity drill: run the escalation steps, output actions and timings.

name: Beds, admissions and discharge
oneLine: One live picture of every bed, admission and discharge across the organisation.
today: Bed state often lives on whiteboards and phone calls. Discharges are often decided late, then wait for medicines, transport or family. Beds can sit empty but not yet cleaned while patients wait elsewhere.
todaySystem: The record system shows who is in each bed, but cleaning status, delay reasons and bed requests are often tracked beside it by phone.
withOspeli: A live bed board shows each bed as occupied, ready, dirty or blocked. Expected discharge dates and delay reasons are logged, and a discharge triggers cleaning, so delays and their reasons are visible.

people.does: Updates bed state on a phone, sets expected discharge dates, records delay reasons.
Matches bed requests to ready beds and proposes moves for the ward to accept.
Records admissions, transfers and discharges with event times.
Tracks patients ready to leave and what each is waiting for.
Runs the bed meeting from the board; sees occupancy, delays and long stays.

screens.name: Bed board
screens.shows: Every bed by ward: occupied, ready, dirty or blocked, with patient code and time in state.

screens.name: My ward (phone)
screens.shows: Ward beds, expected discharge dates, delay reasons and pending admissions, updated in taps.

screens.name: Bed requests
screens.shows: Requests from the emergency department, theatres and transfers, waiting time and bed offered.

screens.name: Discharge tracker
screens.shows: Patients ready to leave, what they wait for: medicines, transport, placement, family.

screens.name: Bed meeting view
screens.shows: Occupancy, expected discharges today, delays over 48 hours and long stays by ward.

captures: Bed requested and bed allocated: measures the wait for a bed.
Admission, transfer and discharge times: drive occupancy and length of stay.
Expected discharge date set or changed: shows planning and slippage.
Ready to leave and actual departure: measures discharge delay.
Delay reason by category: shows what holds discharges.
Bed vacated, cleaned and ready: drives bed turnaround.
Bed blocked or closed, with reason: shows lost capacity.

kpis.name: Bed occupancy
kpis.definition: occupied bed-days / available bed-days
kpis.numerator: Occupied bed-days
kpis.statistic: Average over the period, not a single point in time; any target is an example, set locally
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own
kpis.source: Bagust et al. 1999, BMJ, PMID 10406748, doi:10.1136/bmj.319.7203.155 (risk rises as average occupancy goes above about 85%)

kpis.name: Average length of stay
kpis.definition: inpatient bed-days / discharges in period
kpis.numerator: Inpatient bed-days
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own

kpis.name: Discharges before noon (diagnostic, no target)
kpis.definition: discharges before 12:00 / all discharges; shown to understand the pattern of the day, never as a target
kpis.numerator: Discharges before 12:00
kpis.statistic: Share (%), per period; a diagnostic to understand the pattern of the day, never a target
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own

kpis.name: Discharge delay
kpis.definition: ready to leave → departed, total delayed days and over 48 hours
kpis.numerator: Time between the two events, for each case
kpis.denominator: Cases with both times recorded in the period
kpis.statistic: Total delayed days and over 48 hours
kpis.exclusions: Cases missing either time are not counted; their number is shown beside the result

kpis.name: Long-stay patients
kpis.definition: inpatients with stays of 7 or more and 21 or more days / inpatients
kpis.numerator: Inpatients with stays of 7 or more and 21 or more days
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own
kpis.source: 7 days: the threshold of “more than six days” for a weekly review of long stays, in Guide to reducing long hospital stays (NHS Improvement, June 2018). 21 days: editable default (no published definition confirmed).

guide: When a patient's expected discharge date passes with no delay reason, prompts the ward to record one.
When several patients ready to leave wait for the same thing, such as transport, flags the shared cause to the discharge coordinator.
When bed requests wait and beds sit dirty, suggests which cleans to request first, citing bed requests.
playbooks: Daily bed meeting: review board and delays, output actions with owners.
Long-stay review: list 21-day-plus stays by delay reason, output actions.
methods: Daily senior review with an expected discharge date for every patient (discharge-planning bundle)
Delay-day review (days that move care on versus days spent waiting)

name: Theatres and procedure lists
oneLine: Shows late starts, gaps and on-the-day cancellations, session by session.
today: Lists are often set late and change on the day. Sessions can start late waiting for a bed, a missing tray or staff. Cancellations sometimes happen after patients are prepared, and turnaround time is estimated.
todaySystem: A theatre system holds the list and case times, but late-start reasons and readiness checks for tomorrow often sit outside it.
withOspeli: Lists, sessions and each case's key times are logged in taps. Readiness checks show missing beds, kit or staff the day before, and cancellations carry reasons, so lost session time is visible.

people.does: Builds and changes lists, checks readiness, records cancellations and reasons.
Taps patient in, procedure start, finish and out on a phone.
Sees trays needed per list and flags kit not ready.
Reviews session use, late starts, cancellations and turnaround by theatre.
Sees sessions unused, cancellations for lack of beds, and lists at risk.

screens.name: Today's lists
screens.shows: Each theatre's sessions and cases by patient code, current stage, running late or early.

screens.name: Case times (phone)
screens.shows: Tap into room, anaesthesia start, procedure start, finish, out of room; stamped automatically.

screens.name: Readiness check
screens.shows: Tomorrow's cases: bed, kit, staff and checklist status, gaps highlighted.

screens.name: Session review
screens.shows: Planned versus used time, late start, early finish, turnaround and cancellations per session.

captures: Session planned, released or unused: shows capacity offered and lost.
Patient in room, procedure start and finish, out: measures session use.
Late start with reason: shows what delays the first case.
Cancellation on the day, with reason category: shows avoidable losses.
Out of room to next patient in: measures turnaround.
Tray or kit not ready: links sterile services to delays.
Surgical safety checklist completed, yes or no: tracks completion.

kpis.name: Session utilisation
kpis.definition: time patients in theatre within planned session / planned session time
kpis.numerator: Time patients in theatre within planned session
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own
kpis.counterMeasure: Read with cancellations on the day and overruns past the session end: utilisation alone rewards overbooking

kpis.name: Late starts
kpis.definition: sessions where first case starts after the set window / sessions held
kpis.numerator: Sessions where first case starts after the set window
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own

kpis.name: Cancellations on the day
kpis.definition: cases cancelled on the day / cases listed
kpis.numerator: Cases cancelled on the day
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own

kpis.name: Turnaround time
kpis.definition: patient out of room → next patient in room, median
kpis.numerator: Time between the two events, for each case
kpis.denominator: Cases with both times recorded in the period
kpis.exclusions: Cases missing either time are not counted; their number is shown beside the result

kpis.name: Checklist completion
kpis.definition: cases with the surgical safety checklist recorded complete / cases
kpis.numerator: Cases with the surgical safety checklist recorded complete
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own

guide: When tomorrow's case has no bed booked or kit ready, flags it to the theatre coordinator with the gap.
When sessions are released late repeatedly for a service, suggests a review of session allocation, citing release dates.
When cancellations for one reason rise, suggests a short review of that cause, with the cases listed by code.
playbooks: Session review: compare planned and used time, output lost time by cause.
Cancellation review: group last month's cancellations, output top avoidable causes.

name: Diagnostics: imaging and laboratory
oneLine: Tracks every request, sample and scan from order to reported result.
today: Samples can get lost between ward and laboratory. It is often hard to say when a scan will happen. When an analyser or scanner goes down, wards often find out by phoning. Results can wait to be seen.
todaySystem: Laboratory and imaging systems track the test itself, but the steps before and after, and equipment downtime, are often invisible to the wards.
withOspeli: Requests, specimens and scans carry timestamps at each handoff. Wards see status without phoning, downtime is posted on the board, and turnaround is measured per test and step.

people.does: Sees request status by patient code: collected, received, done, reported.
Scans specimens in, records rejections and reasons, sees the analyser queue.
Sees the scan list, marks scanned and sent for report on a phone.
Reviews turnaround, backlogs, rejections and equipment downtime.
Sees diagnostic waits holding discharges, theatres or the emergency department.

screens.name: Request tracker (phone)
screens.shows: Requests by patient code and stage: ordered, collected, received, done, reported.

screens.name: Specimen log
screens.shows: Specimens received by time and source, rejected with reason, missing after collection.

screens.name: Imaging list
screens.shows: Requests waiting by modality and age, booked slots, scanned and waiting for report.

screens.name: Equipment status
screens.shows: Analysers and scanners up or down, since when, linked work order and expected return.

captures: Request made, with source and urgency set by requester: starts turnaround.
Specimen collected and received in lab: shows transport time and losses.
Specimen rejected, with reason: drives rejection rate and fixes.
Result validated or scan reported: ends turnaround.
Scan booked and performed: measures request to scan.
Analyser or scanner down and back: shows downtime and its impact.
Critical result phoned, time recorded: tracks notification time.

kpis.name: Laboratory turnaround time
kpis.definition: Minutes between "Received at lab" and "Result released", for requests whose result was released in the period, shown for each test group with urgent and routine apart (urgency as set by the requester): the median, and the time 9 in 10 were released within (90th percentile, nearest rank), each with how many results. Received is the tap at the lab hatch; released is the time the lab released the result. There is no headline figure: one figure over every test group and urgency moves when the mix of tests changes, not when the service does. Where one is shown, it is labelled as all test groups and urgencies together, leaves out blood culture, and is not comparable between weeks. Blood culture is reported over days (a first report, then a final one): its row is the time of the first release recorded, never part of a figure across test groups.
kpis.numerator: Requests with a result released in the period that were received at the lab first.
kpis.denominator: None (a median and a percentile, each shown with n).
kpis.statistic: Median and 90th percentile (nearest rank), each with n, by test group, urgent and routine apart
kpis.exclusions: Rejected and cancelled requests (they never reach "Result released"); requests not released yet; releases undone. Blood culture from any figure across test groups. Data completeness and the count of requests received with no collection time are shown beside it.
kpis.source: Editable default (start and end points as set out in Hawkins RC. Laboratory turnaround time. Clin Biochem Rev 2007;28(4):179-94, PMID 18392122; its suggested goal is not adopted)

kpis.name: Request to report (imaging)
kpis.definition: request made → report issued, median by modality
kpis.numerator: Time between the two events, for each case
kpis.denominator: Cases with both times recorded in the period
kpis.exclusions: Cases missing either time are not counted; their number is shown beside the result

kpis.name: Specimen rejection rate
kpis.definition: Specimens rejected, divided by specimens that reached the lab (received plus rejected) in the period, by reason and by source area. A specimen rejected after it was received (for example found by a scientist) counts as rejected, not received. A recollection is a new specimen and counts once on its own.
kpis.numerator: Specimens rejected in the period, at the hatch or after receipt.
kpis.denominator: Specimens that reached the lab in the period: received plus rejected.
kpis.statistic: Share (%), by reason and by source area
kpis.exclusions: Specimens still on the way, cancelled requests. An area with fewer than 10 specimens shows counts, not a percentage (small-number rule, an example setting).
kpis.source: Editable default (in line with the pre-analytical quality indicators of the IFCC working group: Plebani M et al. Clin Chem Lab Med 2015;53(6):943-8, PMID 25719322; Sciacovelli L et al. Clin Chem Lab Med 2017;55(10):1478-88, PMID 28688224; no threshold from them is quoted, and the lab sets its own)

kpis.name: Equipment downtime
kpis.definition: hours down / scheduled hours, per analyser or scanner
kpis.numerator: Hours down
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own

kpis.name: Reporting backlog
kpis.definition: scans performed and not yet reported, by age band
kpis.numerator: Scans performed and not yet reported
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own

guide: When a specimen is collected but not received within the set time, prompts the ward and lab to check it.
When an analyser or scanner goes down, posts the status to affected wards and suggests the agreed backup route.
When rejections for one reason rise from one area, suggests a short review with that area, citing the reasons.
playbooks: Turnaround walk: time a sample's journey, output the longest step.
Downtime drill: rehearse backup routes, output gaps and actions.

standards.name: ISO 15189:2022
standards.how: Turnaround times and specimen rejections are recorded in a form a laboratory can use in its own ISO 15189 quality system.

name: Pharmacy operations
oneLine: Shows medicine stock, expiry dates and dispensing waits, step by step.
today: Stock is often counted by hand and can run out without warning. Discharge medicines are often requested late, so patients wait to go home. Expired stock is often found late.
todaySystem: A pharmacy system holds stock and dispensing records, but wards often cannot see where a request is, so they phone.
withOspeli: Stock levels, top-up points and expiry dates are tracked by location. Dispensing requests are timestamped, so discharge medicine waits show live, and stock-outs are warned before they happen.

people.does: Scans stock in and out, works the dispensing queue, marks ready.
Requests discharge medicines early and sees when they will be ready.
Sees the dispensing queue by request time, checks and releases items.
Reviews stock-outs, expiries, top-up levels and dispensing turnaround.
Sees which planned discharges wait for medicines.

screens.name: Dispensing queue
screens.shows: Requests by ward and request time: received, in progress, checked, ready, collected.

screens.name: Discharge medicines (phone)
screens.shows: For a ward: requests made, expected ready time, ready for collection.

screens.name: Stock levels
screens.shows: Items by location against top-up level, stock-outs, days of stock left.

screens.name: Expiry watch
screens.shows: Items expiring within the set window, by location, with quantity.

captures: Dispensing request received: starts turnaround.
Item checked and ready, then collected: ends turnaround, shows collection wait.
Stock below top-up level: triggers reorder before a stock-out.
Stock-out start and end, by item: drives availability and duration.
Stock expired or wasted: shows avoidable loss.
Stock received from supplier or stores: links to supply delays.

kpis.name: Discharge medicines turnaround
kpis.definition: For discharge requests that reached Ready in the period: the minutes from Raised to Ready on the clock, with time on hold taken out (each On hold to Resumed span), median. The headline is for requests raised inside an example working day (08:00 to 18:00 site time; example setting, not a standard); requests raised outside it are shown apart, with their own median, so an evening request for tomorrow does not stretch the figure. Shown beside it: the median time on hold of the requests that were held, the figure for each planned pick, and "ready before the planned time: n of N" (planned times: this morning 12:00, this afternoon 17:00, this evening 21:00, tomorrow 12:00 the next day; example settings).
kpis.numerator: Discharge requests raised in the working day that reached Ready in the period.
kpis.statistic: Median, time on hold taken out; requests raised outside the working day shown apart
kpis.exclusions: Cancelled requests; requests not ready yet; ward and other requests.

kpis.name: Tracer medicine availability
kpis.definition: tracer items in stock on the day / tracer items listed
kpis.numerator: Tracer items in stock on the day
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own

kpis.name: Stock-out duration
kpis.definition: days out of stock per item, in period
kpis.numerator: Days each item was out of stock
kpis.exclusions: Items not stocked by the site

kpis.name: Expiry value
kpis.definition: value of stock expired / value of stock held, in period
kpis.numerator: Value of stock expired
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own

guide: When stock will reach zero before the next delivery at current use, suggests a reorder quantity for the pharmacy manager.

kpis.exclusions: Cancelled jobs and jobs still open.

kpis.definition: Items passed divided by items checked, for each type of area and for all audits.
kpis.numerator: Items marked pass.
kpis.denominator: Items marked pass or fail in the audits recorded in the period.
kpis.statistic: Share (%), for each type of area and for all audits
kpis.exclusions: Items not checked in an audit.
kpis.source: Your site's cleanliness standard (set locally). The list of items and the types of area here are an example set, not a standard.

kpis.name: Linen stock-outs
kpis.definition: Area-shifts with a linen item at zero divided by area-shifts, for the wards and departments that hold linen. An area-shift is one area for one shift: Day shift 07:00 to 19:00 and night shift 19:00 to 07:00, local time (example setting, set locally). It counts as a stock-out when any linen item there had nothing usable at any time in the shift: a count of zero until the next top-up is issued, or a stock-out a person declared. A top-up counts from when it is issued, which may be before it is on the shelf.
kpis.numerator: Area-shifts in which any linen item was at zero.
kpis.denominator: Area-shifts that began in the period, from each area's first linen record. The shift going on now counts up to now.
kpis.exclusions: The store that supplies the areas, other modules' stock, and areas with no linen record. A shift with no count is not left out and not guessed: it keeps the balance of the last count and the top-ups issued since. A shift nobody counted keeps the last count, so it may hide a stock-out. How many shifts had no count is shown beside the value.

kpis.name: Meal waste
kpis.definition: Meals returned uneaten divided by meals delivered, for each ward, for each meal (breakfast, midday, evening) and in all. Counts only: no patient, no diet, no allergy.
kpis.numerator: Meals returned uneaten.
kpis.denominator: Meals delivered, on the meal records dated in the period (today and the days before it).
kpis.statistic: Share (%), for each ward, for each meal and in all
kpis.exclusions: A ward's meal with no record that day (left out, never counted as zero), and earlier versions of a record that was recorded again (the latest wins).

kpis.name: Transfer wait
kpis.definition: Minutes from a transfer being asked for to the vehicle departing from pickup, for "as soon as possible" requests that departed in the period: the median and the 90th percentile (nearest rank), in all and by request type.
kpis.numerator: As-soon-as-possible journeys that departed from pickup in the period.
kpis.statistic: Median and 90th percentile (nearest rank), in all and by request type
kpis.exclusions: Booked journeys (measured by on-time pickup instead, so a journey booked a day ahead does not look like a long wait); cancelled journeys; journeys not departed yet.

kpis.name: On-time pickup
kpis.definition: Booked journeys whose vehicle arrived at pickup no later than 15 minutes after the booked time, divided by booked journeys due in the period. Arrival at pickup is measured, not departure: departure also waits on the patient and the ward.
kpis.numerator: Booked journeys whose vehicle arrived at pickup within 15 minutes of the booked time, or before it (the window is an example setting, not a standard).
kpis.denominator: Booked journeys whose booked time is in the period. A journey delayed or cancelled for a transport reason (no vehicle, no escort, no crew, vehicle fault, other) counts as not on time; so does one whose vehicle had not arrived when its window closed.
kpis.exclusions: Journeys delayed or cancelled for the requester's reason (patient, paperwork or destination not ready, no longer needed), and journeys whose window has not closed yet. Only a delay or cancellation recorded before the vehicle arrived at pickup (or, with no arrival, before the window closed) is read: one recorded later is about the rest of the journey.

kpis.name: Handover time at destination
kpis.definition: Minutes from the vehicle arriving at the destination to the handover being done: the median and the 90th percentile (nearest rank).
kpis.numerator: Journeys handed over in the period.
kpis.exclusions: Journeys not handed over yet.
kpis.source: Editable default (published definitions of handover delay vary widely: Fouche PF et al., Emerg Med J 2026, PMID 42242732)

kpis.name: Fleet availability
kpis.definition: In-service vehicle-hours divided by scheduled vehicle-hours in the period, in all and by site. Out-of-service time runs between the vehicle being taken out of service and being back in service. Scheduled hours: 07:00 to 19:00 site time every day for each vehicle (an example setting, not a standard).
kpis.numerator: Scheduled vehicle-hours the vehicle was not out of service.
kpis.statistic: Share (%), in all and by site
kpis.exclusions: Hours outside the scheduled hours. Crewed vehicle-hours are shown beside it as their own figure, not folded in.

kpis.name: Acknowledgement time
kpis.definition: Median calendar days from a complaint being received to the site acknowledging it, for complaints acknowledged in the period. Complaints with clinical review count as usual.
kpis.numerator: Calendar days from received to acknowledged, for each complaint acknowledged in the period.
kpis.exclusions: Concerns, compliments and cards are left out.

kpis.name: Response time
kpis.definition: Median calendar days from a complaint being received to the full reply being sent, for complaints replied to in the period.
kpis.numerator: Calendar days from received to replied, for each complaint replied to in the period.
kpis.denominator: Complaints replied to in the period.
kpis.exclusions: A complaint is left out if it was with clinical review at its deciding moment: when the reply was sent, if that was by the reply due date; otherwise at the reply due date. A complaint passed to clinical review after its due date counts as late. Concerns, compliments and cards are left out.

kpis.name: Responses on time
kpis.definition: Complaints replied to by their reply due date, out of complaints whose reply fell due in the period (up to now).
kpis.numerator: Complaints replied to on or before the reply due date.
kpis.denominator: Complaints whose reply due date is in the period and has passed.
kpis.exclusions: A complaint is left out if it was with clinical review at its deciding moment: when the reply was sent, if that was by the reply due date; otherwise at the reply due date. A complaint passed to clinical review after its due date counts as late. Complaints withdrawn before a reply are left out. Concerns, compliments and cards are left out.

kpis.name: Actions closed
kpis.definition: Complaint-linked actions closed by due date / actions due
kpis.numerator: Complaint-linked actions closed by due date
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own

name: Process mapping
oneLine: Maps how work really flows, step by step and role by role.
today: Process maps are often sticky notes from a workshop, with estimated times. It is hard to know which wait is biggest, and changes are often tried on the ward without testing first.
todaySystem: Maps are drawn in a diagram tool, but they hold no times, so they cannot show where the delay is or test a change.
withOspeli: Teams map steps by role with waiting and hands-on time, see where time goes, and test a change on a proposed version first. Phone walk mode is coming, so times are measured.

people.does: Builds the current map with the team and tests a proposed version.
Walks a process on a phone, tapping each step as it happens (coming).
Compares today and proposed maps and decides which change to trial.
Maps the fault-to-fix process and spots handoffs that only pass information.

kpis.name: Total elapsed time
kpis.definition: Process trigger → final step done
kpis.numerator: Time between the two events, for each case
kpis.denominator: Cases with both times recorded in the period
kpis.statistic: Median, with the 90th percentile and n
kpis.exclusions: Cases missing either time are not counted; their number is shown beside the result

kpis.name: Waiting share
kpis.definition: Total waiting time / total elapsed time
kpis.numerator: Total waiting time
kpis.exclusions: None by default; a site adds its own

kpis.name: Handoffs between roles
kpis.definition: Count of steps where the role changes from the step before
kpis.numerator: Steps where the role changes from the step before
kpis.exclusions: None

guide: When one wait is a large share of the whole process, names it and asks what it waits for.
When steps only pass on information after long waits, suggests a one-tap status update instead.
When neighbouring steps by different roles have a long wait, asks if they could run together.
When steps have no times, suggests timing them on the next walk.

name: Playbooks
oneLine: Ready-made routines turn the day's events into the reports operations teams produce.
today: The same flow report, delay summary or business case is often rebuilt from scratch each week, in a different spreadsheet, so results are hard to compare week to week.
todaySystem: A reporting tool produces standard charts, but the analysis and write-up around them are often redone by hand each time.
withOspeli: Each playbook has a fixed input, a fixed analysis and a ready-to-use output, run on the site's own data the same way every time, with each metric's definition beside its number.

people.does: Runs the daily flow report before the morning meeting.
Runs the bottleneck finder on a ward or pathway, reviews ranked delays.
Uses department redesign to compare layout and process options.
Reviews structure reviews and business case packs before executive sign-off.
